classification.difficultyReason: Interpret water depth as adjacent to the angle measured from the vertical and the rope as hypotenuse, then select cosine and calculate; the diagram supplies the construction.

content.prompt: One end of a $12.2\text{ m}$ rope is tied to a boat. The other end is tied to an anchor, which is holding the boat steady in the water. If the rope is making an angle of $34^{\circ}$ with the vertical, how deep is the water? Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: A simple identifiable boat and anchor joined by a rope. Dashed vertical depth and horizontal baseline form a right triangle. The interior angle between the downward vertical and rope is 34 degrees. Decorative illustration details and shading are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The rope is the hypotenuse of length 12.2 m. Water depth is the adjacent side relative to the 34-degree angle at the boat attachment. The vertical and horizontal guides meet at a right angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 12.2 m and 34-degree givens are visible; no depth or calculated answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the water depth. The depth is adjacent to $34^{\circ}$ and the rope is the hypotenuse.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{A}{H}\\\cos34^{\circ}&=\frac{d}{12.2}\\12.2\cos34^{\circ}&=d\\d&\approx10.11\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
